title: Head Lice Prevention and Treatment Reminder
source_title: Bogan Weekly News | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content:
Nurse's 

Notes

Nurse's Notes

Updated December 19th
Dear Parents and Guardians,This is a friendly reminder to please check your child’s hair regularly for head lice. Early detection helps prevent the spread at school. If you notice any signs of lice or nits, please begin treatment promptly and inform the school nurse.In accordance with the CDC we do not need to send students with a head lice infestation home early from school. They can go home at the end of the day, be treated, and return to class after beginning appropriate treatment. The school district follows the CDC guidelines for communicable diseases so please see the attached links below for further information: CDC Head LiceTSD Head Lice Information

summary: Parents are reminded to check their children's hair regularly for **head lice** to help prevent spread at school. If lice or nits are found, begin treatment promptly and notify the school nurse. According to **CDC guidelines**, students with head lice do not need to be sent home early—they can be treated at the end of the day and return to school after beginning appropriate treatment. Resources available: [CDC Head Lice](https://www.cdc.gov/parasites/lice/head/) and TSD Head Lice Information.

title: Cold and Flu Season Guidelines
source_title: Bogan Weekly News | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content:
Nurse's 

Notes

Nurse's Notes

Hi Bogan Families!Cold and flu season are officially here and I wanted to share with you the guidelines on when to keep your sick children at home. This chart touches on more than just cold and flu but is a good reminder to all when we need to stay home and when we are able to return back to school.Please be sure if your child is out sick to call and let our attendance line know they will not be at school. Also, if your child has a doctor's note for excused days, have your child drop that off to the front office.Please click the photo below for information from the CDC.

summary: Cold and flu season is here. Students should stay home with: **fever of 100°F or higher**, **frequent coughing or difficulty breathing**, **diarrhea or vomiting**, **body rash with fever**, **active head lice**, **eye infection with discharge**, or **sore throat with congestion**. Students may return when fever-free for 24 hours without fever-reducing medication, symptoms improve, and specific conditions are met for each illness. If your child is absent due to illness, **call the attendance line** and submit any doctor's notes to the front office.
